headline: Kim Jong-un Accepts Credentials From Russia's New Ambassador
seoTitle: Kim Jong-un Receives Credentials From Russian Ambassador
metaDescription: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un accepted credentials from Russian envoy Andrei Podelyshev, marking a shift in protocol not seen in over three decades.
aiSummaryBullets: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un received diplomatic credentials directly from Russian Ambassador Andrei Podelyshev.
This event represents a significant departure from North Korean diplomatic protocol used over the past 30 years.
The Russian Embassy in Pyongyang confirmed the ceremony took place on Sunday through its official Telegram channel.
aiContextParagraph: Diplomatic protocol in North Korea underwent a notable change on November 22, 2026, when leader Kim Jong-un personally accepted credentials from the new Russian ambassador to the country, Andrei Podelyshev. According to reports from the Russian Embassy in Pyongyang, this direct interaction between the state leader and a foreign envoy is the first of its kind in over three decades. Historically, North Korean leaders have typically refrained from receiving credentials personally from incoming ambassadors, delegating the task to other high-ranking government officials. The timing of this meeting highlights the evolving nature of bilateral relations between Russia and North Korea. While official statements have focused on the procedural shift, the event is considered a departure from established long-term customs governing diplomatic representation in Pyongyang. Both international media outlets confirmed the details of the ceremony following the embassy's announcement.
whyItIsViral: The story is being tracked by two independent news outlets, reflecting the significance of this shift in North Korean diplomatic protocol.
